title: FMTS — Forge Module Test Specification
description: What every Forge module declares before a hub admits it: its kind, the baseline it claims (M-1 to M-11), its time contract, references to its other specs, and waivers. Decided in docs/decisions/forge-module-requirements.md (D-12, signed 2026-11-17). One spec per module, `<module>.fmts.json`.

spec_version.description: FMTS schema version this spec is written against.

module_identity.description: What the module is and where its source lives.

module_id.description: Unique kebab-case id of the module.

alias.description: The module's shortcut name (owner, 2026-11-18): short, lower case, unique among the modules. Where a person or a command names a module briefly, this is the name (`wms` for `forge-wms`).

kind.description: management: a forge-<service> module that runs a business function (forge-mes, forge-wms, forge-cmms). integration: a module whose counterpart is third-party software; the only place that system's API is called (A-4, O-5). ot: the module that talks to plant-floor devices. display: forge-display, the one module that renders user interfaces (A-3).

language.description: The language the module is written in. Modules are Go (A-2); python is the hub-hosted adapters and the OT module; typescript is the interim MES bridge only.

source_paths.description: Repository-relative directories that hold the module's source. The static checks read these.

hub_link.description: M-1: the module speaks forge.v1.AdapterService to its hub over gRPC and nothing else.

references.description: The module's other declarations. FMTS names them and requires them; it does not repeat them.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the FACTS spec.

adapter_id.description: The adapter_id the FACTS spec and the manifest carry.

manifest.description: M-2: repository-relative path of the manifest the module registers with.

fvts.description: M-9: repository-relative paths of the module's FVTS specs, one per view contract.

roles.description: M-10: repository-relative path of the module's shipped roles (roles record R-12): a JSON file with a `roles` list, each a `role_id`, its `scopes` and the roles it `inherits`.

baseline.description: The claim for each of the eleven requirements: met, or waived by an entry in `waivers`. A requirement with no waiver is enforced in full.

waivers.description: Requirements this module cannot yet meet (Q-8). The owner approves each through the spec's hash; the runner reports every waiver on every run.

time_contract.description: M-3: one entry for every counterpart the module exchanges data with. Every entry fails closed.

hub.description: The link to the hub. Its tolerance class is the one the FACTS spec declares in `time_governance`; it is not repeated here.

exchange.description: The exchange carried on every Register, Health and Ingest (one-clock record P-9).

plant_floor_devices.description: none: the module talks to no plant-floor device or server. declared-in-facts: it does, and the FACTS spec's `time_governance` (and its `connections`) is the declaration.

databases.description: Every database the module reads or writes (Q-5).

third_party_systems.description: Every third-party system the module calls. An integration module has at least one (O-6).

user_interface.description: M-9: a module ships no user interface code; it describes its screens in FVTS specs and forge-display renders them (A-3). The display module is the one kind this does not bind.

ships_ui_code.description: True when the module's source contains user interface code.

screens.description: True when the module has screens; then `references.fvts` names their view contracts.

scaffold.description: M-11: the module SDK template the module was built from.

template.description: python-adapter: the six-file layout `forge module init` generates. go-module: the Go layout of docs/decisions/forge-mes-go.md. none: not built from a template; M-11 must then be waived.

metadata.description: Free-form context for people. Not enforced.

integrity.description: Self-contained spec integrity block (FHTS Layer 1). Hash governance for AI agent oversight.

spec_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of canonical JSON (excluding this field).

hash_state.description: Governance state — tracks whether changes have been reviewed and approved.

previous_hash.description: Hash before most recent change. Enables single-step drift detection.

approved_by.description: Identifier of actor who approved current hash state.

change_history.description: Last 3 hash changes for audit trail and AI agent governance.

toleranceClass.description: The tolerance classes of the one-clock record (P-8). Mirrors FACTS `time_governance.tolerance_class`; the runner fails if they drift.

reason.description: Why the module cannot meet the requirement today.

backlog_item.description: The open BACKLOG.md item that removes the waiver. A waiver whose item is closed or missing fails.

owner.description: hub: a database the hub owns (A-6); the hub checks its clock. third-party: the database of a third-party system; the integration module measures its clock and reports the offset. module: a database the module holds itself, which M-8 forbids.

credential.description: Who issued the credential the module connects with (M-8).

written_time_source.description: Which governed clock the times the module writes come from. Required when the module writes. The database's own now() is not a permitted source (Q-5).

clock_read_method.description: Third-party databases: how the module reads the server's clock.

offset_reported.description: Third-party databases with a readable clock: the module corrects the database's times to master time and reports the offset on the record (Q-5).

polling_interval_seconds.description: When the clock is unreadable: the module's read time is the stamp and this interval is recorded as the uncertainty on every record (Q-6).

interface.description: How the module reaches the system (rest, graphql, amqp, mqtt, file, …).

clock_read_method.description: How the module reads the system's clock. unreadable is a declaration, not an escape: it requires `polling_interval_seconds` (Q-6).

offset_reported.description: Readable clocks: the offset is reported on the record.

polling_interval_seconds.description: When the clock is unreadable: the uncertainty recorded on every record.
